body:
This PR fixes a lot of small CSS-Issues and improves the cpu and memory charts.


## Charts
I've updated the chart library to the latest version and added a tooltip that displays the cpu / ram usage at the point of time where the cursor hovers over the chart. Additionally the cpu chart and legend show the usage now in percent (instead of 0 to cpu count) and has its y max fixed at 100%. author: robxnano
body:
I'm trying to improve the metainfo which shows in app stores and Flathub, in order to bring it into line with the Flathub [quality guidelines](https://docs.flathub.org/docs/for-app-authors/metainfo-guidelines/quality-guidelines/). One of the new requirements is for brand colors which are used in app tiles. Would anyone like to take a look or offer suggestions on what colors would be appropriate? Since the HandBrake logo doesn't have a single predominant color there's no obvious color to use.

I've also added the latest patch notes in preparation for the next release.

**Tested on:**

- [ ] Windows 10+  (via MinGW)
- [ ] macOS 10.13+
- [x] Ubuntu Linux

**Screenshots**

For reference, this is how the tile looks with the placeholder colors I picked. The light and dark colors don't necessarily have to be a similar hue as they aren't used together.

```tsx

  !request.data ||
  downloadingContext.request.segment.externalId !== command.i ||
  downloadingContext.requestId !== command.r;
```

author: limerio
body: Initially, I was investigating why the format of expiresAt is a date (format: `YYYY-MM-DD`). What seemed unusual was that while the expiration time is set to one hour later, the expiresAt field doesn't include any time information. To address this, I attempted to convert it to a timestamp (which I think, it's not the best approach, as it converts all dates to timestamps – feel free to contribute and improve this solution). However, I encountered another issue: when you call `new Date()`, it returns a date in your machine's local timezone rather than UTC. Therefore, I needed to convert it to UTC to ensure that both the timestamp and UTC time were in the same timezone.

author: cheyennewills
body:
When building with lto (Link Time Optimization) flags, the compiler discovered an inconsistency in the datatypes for the structures:
    BbScan, Bescan, Bfield, Blimit, and Bllist.

    [gcc-15] data.r: error: type of Bllist does not match original
        declaration [-Werror=lto-type-mismatch]

In rmacros.h, the macro OpBlock produces a structure definition of:

    struct b_iproc B{name} ...

In grttin.h the macro LibDcl is uses OpBlock to define structures.

The definitions for the structures BbScan, Bescan, Bfield, Blimit, and Bllist are generated in imisc.r and omisc.r via LibDcl's or OpBlock's.

However in data.r, the datatype for these structures are declared as struct b_proc.

To fix the lto problem, change the data type of the externs and the datatype of the opblks array to be b_iproc instead of b_proc so they properly match the datatypes in imisc and omisc.

Note this problem was discovered via gentoo's QA processing (see https://bugs.gentoo.org/940325)

## Summary

Several endpoints for retrieving files were removed, and a new object `NestedTaskEventModel` was added, along with a new tag `EntityFiles`.

### Removed

- The following endpoints were removed:
  - `/comments/{commentId}/allfiles`
  - `/companies/{companyId}/allfiles`
  - `/projecttemplates/{projecttemplateId}/allfiles`
  - `/tasks/{taskId}/allfiles`
  - `/users/{userId}/allfiles`
  - `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/allfiles`

### Added

- A new OpenAPI object `NestedTaskEventModel` was added.
- A new tag `EntityFiles` was added to the `/projects/{projectId}/allfiles` endpoint.

### Changed

- The description of the `/projects/{projectId}/allfiles` endpoint was updated to include all files from tasks linked to the project.
- The `userIds` and `guids` parameters in the `/users/{userId}/workload` endpoint were changed to accept a list of GUIDs as a comma-separated string.
- The `GuidList` object was removed as it is no longer used.

No other changes were made.

- Replaced placeholder data with an empty graph for better visuals.

- Upload Model:
  - Added a button/input field for users to upload model files.
  - Implemented validation for file format and size.
  - Successfully displays the uploaded model in the model list.
  
- Delete Model:
  - Added a delete button for each uploaded model.
  - Prompted for confirmation before deleting a model.
  - Removed the model from the list and server after confirmation.

- API Integration:
  - Integrated API calls for uploading and deleting models.
  - Showed success or error messages based on the upload and delete actions.

- Local Storage:
  - Stored models and their data in local storage.
  - Persisted models in the list after a page reload.
  - Removed deleted models from local storage.

- User Feedback:
  - Provided clear success or error messages for upload and delete actions.
  - Included loading indicators during file upload and deletion processes.

author: snendev
body:
# Issue

#34 - Refactor to allow users to trigger capture/playback as-needed

This is an extension of #36 using observers.

# Changes

The solution here is very similar to #36 except that, because Observers are used to trigger the initialization of playback and startup, the systems that previously initialized the behavior are now observer systems. This means they don't have to be ordered, which I suppose is nice.

In the future I'd like to explore how reasonable it would be to spawn entities that handle the playback/capture rather than spawning resources, e.g. in case users wanted to record multiple windows simultaneously or store captures in the world for later playback/editing.

# Questions

Which approach is preferred?

# TODOs

- Still would like help auditing the test suite and either adding or suggesting whatever new tests are appropriate.

        - Will be letters if there is no Profile picture
        - Dependent on some daisyUI features

    - Added new type for passing along className and image className to a component (under classChange)

body:
when commands fail, they often print error messages to stderr. previously, failures were quite hard to debug because tmux would hide stderr.

before:
```
; tmux run-shell 'echo oops >&2; exit 1'
'echo oops >&2; exit 1' returned 1
```

after:
```
; tmux run-shell 'echo oops >&2; exit 1'
oops
'echo oops >&2; exit 1' returned 1
```

author: dartvanya
body:
### General
- Theme can be changed at `runtime w/o restart` by `EnableThemeSupport` and `EnableThemeUseWindowsTheme`. All PH/PV windows and dialogs will be redrawed automatically.
- If `EnableThemeUseWindowsTheme` enabled theme will be `switched automatically` when Windows theme is changing.
- Streamer mode, acrylic, theme custom colors settings are applied immediately on all windows w/o restart.
- New option `EnableThemeUseWindowsTheme` - `Use Windows app color mode`. On default settings PH will use current Windows theme.

---
### phlib and other UI fixes
- Moved delayhook to phlib.
- phlib `PhIsThemeSupportEnabled`, `PhReInitializeTheme`, `PhReInitializeStreamerMode`. Exported for plugins.
- New option `EnableThemeTabBorders` (default 0).
- TreeNew: fix custom `ForeColor` for dark mode.

---
### SDK
- `hndlprp.h`. Removed duplicate declarations for plugins. Consolidated handle property APIs in public part of header.
- Add some missing declarations and exports of `IListView` wrappers.
- Update `objmgr` and `objprp` code to latest SDK.
---

> If AppMode is set to PreferredAppModeDarkOnDark, PhShouldAppsUseDarkMode should return current Windows app color mode.
> It's weird that sometimes it can return incorrect inverted value (idk why).
> In this case use PhGetAppsUseLightTheme() to retrieve raw value from registry.
> 
> When app mode set to always dark/light all subsequent calls to PhShouldAppsUseDarkMode always ignore
> the current Windows app color mode. Possible return values are:

| PreferredAppMode | PhShouldAppsUseDarkMode return  | PhGetAppsUseLightTheme return
| ------------- |:-------------:|:-------------:|
| PreferredAppModeDisabled           | current Windows app color mode  | current Windows app color mode |
| PreferredAppModeDarkOnDark     | current Windows app color mode   | current Windows app color mode |
| PreferredAppModeDarkAlways      | always TRUE     | current Windows app color mode |
| PreferredAppModeLightAlways      | always FALSE   | current Windows app color mode |

author: navacharleshorowitz
body:
Based on 10/21/2024 security incident in which a logfile in project tmp/ was inadvertently committed and pushed to a branch (and caught by github secret scanning as containing a logged license key), updated .gitignore to ignore all contents in project tmp/ directory, but to create an empty directory (with .keep placeholder) to support local tmp work as necessary.

## 🎫 Ticket

This ticket provides the relevant background. No separate ticket was opened for the update of the gitignore, which was discussed in post-mortem.
https://jira.cms.gov/browse/DPC-4341


## 🛠 Changes

.gitignore was updated to ignore all tmp/ contents except tmp/.keep
tmp/.keep was added to pre-establish a tmp directory in the repo to be used as necessary without its contents being included in commits.

## ℹ️ Context

Change was made to permit typical uses of tmp directory in local development without accidentally committing contents to github


## 🧪 Validation

Verified that files added to tmp/ (except empty placeholder .keep) are ignored for staging commits.

author: see1duck
body:
# Changelog 

### New Plugin

- **Aerial Fisher Plugin**
  - *A new fully automated fishing plugin that does aerial fishing at Molch Island.*

### Changes and Improvements

#### API Classes

- **Rs2Npc**
  - *Log message "Natural mouse is not enabled, can't hover" is now only shown when the devDebug flag is enabled.*

- **NaturalMouse**
  - *Method `moveTo` now checks if the mouse is already at the destination before moving, and returns immediately if it is, instead of wasting resources trying to move the mouse.*
  - *Method `moveOffScreen` is now triggering 100% of the time when called, instead of the previous hardcoded 25% chance.*
  - *Method `moveOffScreen` now has a overload option to specify the percentage chance of moving off screen.*

- **Rs2Random**
  - *Method `waitEx` has been fixed to properly calculate the wait time inside the given range.*

- **Rs2Inventory**
  - *Method `getRandom(int... itemIDs)` now actually returns a random item from the list of item IDs, instead of always returning the first item.*
  - *Method `getRandom(String... itemNames)` now actually returns a random item from the list of item names, instead of always returning the first item.*
  - *Method `getRandom(Predicate<Rs2Item> itemFilter)` now actually returns a random item that matches the filter, instead of always returning the first item.*
  - *New method `hover(Rs2Item item)` moves the mouse to hover over the specified item in the inventory. Returns false if natural mouse isn't enabled or the item is null.*

- **Rs2GameObject**
  - *Log message "Natural mouse is not enabled, can't hover" is now only shown when the devDebug flag is enabled.*

- **Rs2Bank**
  - *Log message "Natural mouse is not enabled, can't hover" is now only shown when the devDebug flag is enabled.*

- **Rs2Antiban**
  - *Method `moveMouseOffScreen` has been updated to use the new `NaturalMouse.moveOffScreen` method.*
  - *New Setting `moveMouseOffScreenChance` has been added to specify the percentage chance of moving the mouse off screen.*
  - *UI now have the `moveMouseOffScreenChance` setting in the Antiban tab to allow users to set the chance of moving the mouse off screen.*



## **Plugins**

- **QoL Plugin**
  - **New Fletching Section**
    - Added multiple options to enhance the fletching experience:
      - **Quick Fletch Items**: Allows quick fletching of logs into selected items with one click on the knife.
      - **Fletching Item Selection**: Choose which item to fletch from logs (e.g., Arrow Shafts).
      - **Quick Fletch Darts**: Enables rapid fletching of darts. *(Note: The make-x setting must be disabled for this to work.)*
      - **Quick Fletch Arrows**: Allows quick assembly of arrows with one click on any type of arrowhead.
      - **Quick Fletch Bolts**: Enables rapid fletching of bolts. *(Note: The make-x setting must be disabled for this to work.)*
      - **Quick Fletch Headless Arrows**: Streamlines the creation of headless arrows with one click on the arrow shafts.
  - **Dialogue Section**
    - Added support for handling quest dialogues. The plugin will now automatically handle quest dialogues and select the correct options. *(Note: This feature relies on the Quest Helper plugin to highlight the correct dialogue options.)*
  - **Removed Settings**
    - Removed the `Auto Run` setting due to the official client's recent update that added the feature.

- **Fletcher Plugin**
  - *Banking logic has been changed to remove most of the sleep calls in between each action that was causing the plugin to be slow and robotic.*
  - *Banking logic now utilizes the mouse movement as a non-blocking and natural delay between actions and allows the plugin to be faster and have a more human-like flow. It performs a single final check at the end of the banking process to ensure all items are withdrawn before continuing.*

Except for the added (and sorted) includes, and the removal of redundant parentheses, this patch can be approximated with the following semantic patch:

	$ cat ~/tmp/spatch/streq.sp;
	@@
	expression a, b;
	@@

	- strcmp(a, b) == 0
	+ streq(a, b)

	@@
	expression a, b;
	@@

	- 0 == strcmp(a, b)
	+ streq(a, b)

	@@
	expression a, b;
	@@

	- !strcmp(a, b)
	+ streq(a, b)

	$ find contrib/ lib* src/ -type f \
	| xargs spatch --sp-file ~/tmp/spatch/streq.sp --in-place;
	$ git restore lib/string/strcmp/streq.h;

---

author: prisci-martinez
body:
This project implements several key features to enhance the structural monitoring system for buildings. The system is designed to detect abnormal vibrations and humidity levels, analyze structural conditions, and provide user-friendly alerts and interfaces.

# Implemented Features:

## Vibration Detection:

The system uses a vibration sensor connected to the ADC to detect abnormal movements and vibrations that may indicate a potential collapse.
Implemented functions to read vibration data and compare it against predefined thresholds to determine the severity of vibrations. Also, the frequency of vibrations is calculated due to the importance of this parameter in the health of the structures.

### Humidity Detection:

The system measures humidity levels inside walls and floors using a humidity sensor connected to the ADC.
Implemented functions to read humidity data and log it for further analysis.

### Risk Alert:

The system alerts through a buzzer if the user does not address structural issues within a certain time frame.
The buzzer is controlled using PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) to generate the alert sound.

### Data Analysis:

The system analyzes recorded information over time to assess the structure's condition based on humidity levels and the frequency of seismic events.

### User-Friendly Interface:

The system includes a LED system or panel displaying the building’s structural status, with a color-coded system (green, yellow, red) to indicate safety levels.
Implemented functions to update LED statuses based on the analyzed data.

### Manual Alarm Activation:

The system includes a switch connected to a GPIO port to manually activate and deactivate the alarm.
Implemented an interrupt service routine (ISR) to handle the switch input for manual alarm control.

### DMA:

The system uses DMA to efficiently transfer data between peripherals and the program memory.

# Code :
### Vibration Detection:

Added functions in adc.c and common.c to read and process vibration data.

### Humidity Detection:

Added functions in adc.c and common.c to read and process humidity data.

### Risk Alert:

Added alert mechanism in common.c.

### Analysis:

Added data analysis algorithms in common.c and main.c

### User-Friendly Interface:

Implemented LED status update functions in common.c and main.c.

### Manual Alarm Activation:

Added ISR for manual alarm control in main.c.

### DMA:

Added DMA feature for moving data from ADC channels to memory space that is accessible for the main program.
Configuration

### Platformio.ini:
Ensured necessary libraries and settings are included for the STM32F103C8 platform.

# Continuous Integration:

We configured GitHub Actions to automate the process of building, style, and documentation of our code.
We implemented workflows that run automatically with each commit or pull request, ensuring the system is always tested and functioning correctly.
The actions include:
Verifying the project build to ensure code integrity.
Checking code style using clang-format to maintain consistent formatting.
Ensuring the presence and correctness of documentation generated with Doxygen.


# Conclusion
This project enhances the structural monitoring system by implementing critical features for vibration and humidity detection, risk alerts, analysis, and user-friendly interfaces. These improvements ensure a robust and reliable system for monitoring building structures and alerting users to potential risks.

We included a video demonstration to showcase the system's functionality [here](https://youtu.be/dYDfKD5cJ_Q?si=eoCJy7TubDWJd_nS).

body:
This pull request includes significant updates to the Golang-based REST API for managing workout programs. The changes involve a major restructuring of the project directory, enhancements to the OAuth authentication flow, and updates to the README file to reflect these changes.

### Project Restructuring:
* Updated the directory structure to follow Go best practices, moving files to `cmd`, `internal`, and `pkg` directories. (`README.md`, [README.mdL27-R52](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L27-R52))
* Renamed and refactored several files, including `controllers/exercise_controller.go` to `internal/controllers/exercise_controller.go`, and added new files for user controllers and OAuth logic. (`internal/controllers/exercise_controller.go`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-530467b3e85c1de32541666e00d0a9da9c369989be546e6540371768b0653298L8-R9); `internal/auth/oauth.go`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-046f4ed0789b62e02dfe7f6f997d386dc04ab8aa89637b0c61bd8e08868848edR1-R167)

### OAuth Authentication:
* Implemented a new OAuth authentication flow with Google, including handlers for login, callback, and logout. (`internal/auth/oauth.go`, [internal/auth/oauth.goR1-R167](diffhunk://#diff-046f4ed0789b62e02dfe7f6f997d386dc04ab8aa89637b0c61bd8e08868848edR1-R167))
* Removed the old `auth/oauth.go` file and replaced it with a more secure and comprehensive OAuth implementation. (`auth/oauth.go`, [auth/oauth.goL1-L48](diffhunk://#diff-834b89e7e0bcaf377290218d4f47b9424bfbab7b3ee55cf537405f99530729b7L1-L48))

### README Updates:
* Updated the README to include new sections for environment setup, API endpoints, and directory structure. (`README.md`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L80-R100) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L175-L235)
* Reformatted the API endpoints section to use a table for better readability. (`README.md`, [README.mdL175-L235](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L175-L235))

### Database Configuration:
* Refactored the database connection logic and moved it to `internal/database/db.go`. (`internal/database/db.go`, [internal/database/db.goR1-R69](diffhunk://#diff-d18caea19014a2e48b9dc31a7831f7a43b1c3068421642110862803da915e00dR1-R69))
* Added functions to store user information in the database after OAuth login. (`internal/database/db.go`, [internal/database/db.goR1-R69](diffhunk://#diff-d18caea19014a2e48b9dc31a7831f7a43b1c3068421642110862803da915e00dR1-R69))

### Miscellaneous:
* Added a new `cmd/main.go` file to handle environment selection and server startup. (`cmd/main.go`, [cmd/main.goR1-R90](diffhunk://#diff-c444f711e9191b53952edb65bfd8c644419fc7695c62611dc0fb304b4fb197d6R1-R90))
* Updated the `go.mod` file to include new dependencies for JWT and OAuth. (`go.mod`, [go.modR14](diffhunk://#diff-33ef32bf6c23acb95f5902d7097b7a1d5128ca061167ec0716715b0b9eeaa5f6R14))

These changes enhance the overall structure, security, and functionality of the project, making it more maintainable and scalable.

This codemod will set Django's `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` flag to `True` if it's `False` or missing on the `settings.py` file within Django's default directory structure.

```diff
+ SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True
```

Setting this flag on ensures that the session cookies are only sent under an HTTPS connection. Leaving this flag off may enable an attacker to use a sniffer to capture the unencrypted session cookie and hijack the user's session.

author: nabhag8848
body:
🔥 Twenty Raycast Integration

Twenty simplifies CRM management, empowering businesses to enhance productivity and drive growth. With this Raycast integration, record creation across standard and custom objects is now at your fingertips, making your workflow effortless and efficient. Experience how easy it is to use this Raycast for seamless record creation! ## $\{\textcolor{#39FF14}{\textbf{🤝 Create records instantly across Standard and Custom Objects!}}}$ ## Command Descriptions ### Create Object Record With `Create Object Record` command, effortlessly create records in any standard or custom object. Search command press Enter to see active objects, then press `CMD + Enter` to unveil a form that fills in your record seamlessly into the CRM table — making CRM magic happen! --- ## Getting Started Get your API Keys from [twenty developer settings](https://twenty.com/settings/developers) , navigate to Raycast Command settings or try to access command which will open up view to provide your API key.
if you are selfhost user navigate to `/settings/developers`, once you have your key, go to Raycast Command Settings to provide your `selfhost api url` and `API key`. If you don't provide selfhost url, Integration will assume [https://api.twenty.com](https://api.twenty.com) as your instance.
--- ## User Guide To use the integration, search for the `Create Object Record` command, which will display all your `active` standard and custom objects currently in your twentyCRM. Its very flexible - if you create new objects or deactivate existing ones, this will automatically reflect those changes. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fca0f71d-3c04-43ad-afb4-4e5b0a9d4d13 When you deactivate any standard or custom object, it will no longer appear, ensuring you only see the information and objects you want to access. This makes the integration extensible and enhances your productivity. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f357b91b-dd2e-4043-af8c-9328235c0aa8 If you create new custom objects, they will appear, allowing you to quickly create your records instantly from Raycast. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0d8fa96-468b-42e4-a11c-a9e4a47ce412 To create a record for any object, select your target object and press `ENTER`. This will open a form that matches the exact table schema you created in your CRM, following any validations it suggests to successfully create your record by pressing `CMD + ENTER`. Records cannot be created with an empty first column (such as Name, Title, etc.). https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f8d7127-63a6-4113-ac6a-5ea3003c5f0c Similar to creation of standard object record you can create custom objects record https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/098e120c-ac58-4f41-9560-2782c798d6bd If you want to create multiple records for the same object without closing the form after each one, go to the Raycast command settings and check the option to `keep object form open after record creation`.
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d87ca8e-c7b2-4962-b427-947220bcbb86 It's much more flexible—similar to objects, if you deactivate any fields, they will no longer appear in your object schema during record creation. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2686c7c0-dfde-4445-93be-17d10cf22d60 No worries! If you add or update any fields in your standard objects, they will automatically appear in your object schema form in Raycast, looking closely you will see, if you add a select field with a default value provided some icon, it will display exactly what you’ve set when creation. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/697da72b-1ca2-4493-b61c-d393b77b34f6 ## 🧑‍💻 Contributing Contributions are what make the open source community such an amazing place to learn, inspire, and create. Any contributions you make are **greatly appreciated**. If you have a suggestion that would make this better, please fork the repo and create a pull request. You can also simply open an issue. Don't forget to give the project a star! Thanks again! 1. Fork the Project 2. Create your Feature Branch (`git checkout -b feat/AmazingFeature`) 3. Install Dependency (`npm install`) & follow getting started guide for api key. 4. Commit your Changes (`git commit -m 'feat: adds some amazing feature'`) 5. Push to the Branch (`git push origin feat/AmazingFeature`) 6. Open a Pull Request ## 💬 Connect With Me
| **Name** | Nabhag Motivaras | |:--------------------|:-------------------| | **Twitter** | [@NabhagMotivaras](https://x.com/NabhagMotivaras) |
## Support my work If you love my work and would like to support me, consider becoming a [GitHub sponsor](https://github.com/sponsors/Nabhag8848) ## Roadmap - [x] Currently we support `FULL_NAME`, `TEXT`, `LINKS`, `EMAILS`, `SELECT`. - [x] Supporting other fields are easy as we have build the foundation and its quite similar to what we have already build. - [ ] PHONE_NUMBER, CURRENCY similar to LINKS - [ ] RATING (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 as option), BOOLEAN (True or False as option), MULTI_SELECT are similar to SELECT - [ ] RELATION Similar to SELECT but requires additional work but doable - [ ] support seeing records of all objects ## Checklist - [x] I read the [extension guidelines](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store) - [x] I read the [documentation about publishing](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/publish-an-extension) - [x] I ran `npm run build` and [tested this distribution build in Raycast](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store#metadata-and-configuration) - [x] I checked that files in the `assets` folder are used by the extension itself - [x] I checked that assets used by the `README` are placed outside of the `metadata` folder

body:
# Scroll and other fixes

Several small changes in the UI.

## Changes made

- When a chat loads or a new message is added to the chat, it scrolls to the latest text (non-location) message
- The border radius of the side panel is now consistent with the Figma
- `location` database entries with empty values for `rating` are now parsed correctly, and `(No rating)` is shown if it's empty (this was previously causing HTTP 500 errors)
- Fixed a bug where a long URL would cause the location info panel to become wider than its container

author: jianqi02
body:
### The addressed issue
**1. Code Redundancy**
The original code contains some redundant logic, and these redundant logic has made the whole code become hard to be read and understand.

**2. Code Duplication**
The original code contains some duplicated code in string formatting which make the code become difficult to be maintained.

**3. Simplifying the logic**
The original code contains some complex nested if-statement which can be avoided.

### What you have reengineered
**1. Refactor Long Methods**
For the module Chart, there are some methods are lengthy and handle multiple responsibilities such as data processing, setting axis, adding bars, and managing labels. These responsibilities could be split into smaller, more focused methods.

**2. Eliminate Code Duplication**
The logic for checking Python dependencies has a lot of repeated patterns. I have abstracted this into a single function that handles all dependency types and passes in arguments such as the dependency list and error or warning messages.

**3. Encapsulate File I/O Operations**
For the update checking method, the function includes direct file handling and parsing. It can be abstracted into separate I/O operations and parsing logic functions, which will make it easier to handle errors and test the logic separately.

**4. Constant Reassignments**
For the module Parser, the class assigns self.C multiple times, which can be simplified by ensuring it's initialized once in the constructor.

**5. Complex Code Simplification**
The complex nested loops for iterating over databases and tables for the admin layout can be simplified with better indentation and clearer conditions.

### Reengineering strategy or approach used 
**1. Refactoring**
I have improving the code without changing its external behavior using refactoring. This approach will focus on making the code more readable, maintainable, and efficient. For example, refactoring is used when eliminating the code redundancy and code duplication, and also simplify the complex code like nested loop and nested if statement. After applying this approach, the code will become more easy to be read by other programmers. Besides, with modular and organized code, future modifications, debugging, and enhancements will be faster and less error-prone.

**2. Forward Engineering**
Forward engineering is the process of improving or rewriting parts of the system based on the knowledge gained from reverse engineering and refactoring. I have improving some parts of the code to introduce better structures by simplifying the algorithm used. It involves redesigning parts of the system for better future maintainability. Forward engineering involved redesigning parts of the system for better future extensibility. 

### Impact of changes
**1. Better Testing and Coverage**
The refactored code is more modular and better segmented. It makes the unit tests written for individual components become more easier. This leads to improved test coverage and higher confidence in the stability of the codebase. Besides, when code is simpler, tests become easier to write and understand.

**2. The Code Quality is Improved**
The readability of the code is increased. From the refactoring, it makes the code easier to read and understand. By improving naming conventions, removing redundancies, and organizing the structure, future developers or other people can navigate and comprehend the codebase more easily. Furthermore, the simplified and cleaner code is easier to maintain.

body:
This pull request includes several changes to the `MiFarma` project, focusing on adding file writing functionality and updating file handling methods. The most important changes include the addition of methods to write data to files, updates to file handling in the `ControllerProgram` class, and renaming of files to reflect their purpose better.

### File Writing Functionality:
* [`MiFarma/Boleta.h`](diffhunk://#diff-e9a25d92600e56c741edbb6bbb1ff50f026bdd4e585c69c18c65c52b55463d06R68-R77): Added `escribirArchivo` method to write `Boleta` details to a file.
* [`MiFarma/Empleado.h`](diffhunk://#diff-475e74b6a6345bc06fd666cb5c2bde7a9104bf6e44151ec240e5808610aee866R45-R59): Added `escribirArchivo` method to write `Empleado` details to a file.
* [`MiFarma/Pedido.h`](diffhunk://#diff-fbd9f22a9eff252028033d9afd6dd9cdee61c970c8c6fbfcb4efe6f23188719aR125-R141): Added `escribirArchivo` method to write `Pedido` details to a file.
* [`MiFarma/Producto.h`](diffhunk://#diff-4544ab3d4686bed434a77436bb7f1e65a9cbd3e4a0036a6d4d29a990205302b4R70-R81): Added `escribirArchivo` method to write `Producto` details to a file.
* [`MiFarma/Proveedor.h`](diffhunk://#diff-a1634d9124e04287b5952a730bb33855931364d258574eb586388c70e284ef1aR46-R55): Added `escribirArchivo` method to write `Proveedor` details to a file.
* [`MiFarma/Reclamos.h`](diffhunk://#diff-c0f8c63ccf05510c4ff33d84cfe07b11d60c2e2bffd286ffb827d49dfc63bee9L108-R122): Added `escribirArchivo` method to write `Reclamo` details to a file.
* [`MiFarma/Usuario.h`](diffhunk://#diff-8ff3bf3fe10980b6c94e1a11339fc4102d8ee01dbf2584d4fed4e137df8e4206R44-R57): Added `escribirArchivo` method to write `Usuario` details to a file.

### File Handling Updates:
* [`MiFarma/ControllerProgram.h`](diffhunk://#diff-29fc911f28d195f7a797354cd5989f6b4550c2c54c9d17ff74c8ddcb99129a94L130-R130): Updated file opening methods to use new file names for reading operations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-29fc911f28d195f7a797354cd5989f6b4550c2c54c9d17ff74c8ddcb99129a94L130-R130) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-29fc911f28d195f7a797354cd5989f6b4550c2c54c9d17ff74c8ddcb99129a94L166-R166) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-29fc911f28d195f7a797354cd5989f6b4550c2c54c9d17ff74c8ddcb99129a94L197-R197) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-29fc911f28d195f7a797354cd5989f6b4550c2c54c9d17ff74c8ddcb99129a94L231-R231) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-29fc911f28d195f7a797354cd5989f6b4550c2c54c9d17ff74c8ddcb99129a94L263-R263) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-29fc911f28d195f7a797354cd5989f6b4550c2c54c9d17ff74c8ddcb99129a94L295-R295)
* [`MiFarma/ControllerProgram.h`](diffhunk://#diff-29fc911f28d195f7a797354cd5989f6b4550c2c54c9d17ff74c8ddcb99129a94R414-R472): Added `actualizarLogistica` method to write updated data to respective files. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-29fc911f28d195f7a797354cd5989f6b4550c2c54c9d17ff74c8ddcb99129a94R414-R472) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-29fc911f28d195f7a797354cd5989f6b4550c2c54c9d17ff74c8ddcb99129a94R508)

### File Renaming:
* `MiFarma/ListaEmpleados.txt` renamed to `MiFarma/LecturaListaEmpleados.txt`.

### Miscellaneous:
* [`MiFarma/Libreria.h`](diffhunk://#diff-054e5ebb928493caaab7e20a27156116d62f003e4169687b02012084b934db05L17-R33): Defined new file names for reading and writing operations.
* [`MiFarma/VistaEmpleado.h`](diffhunk://#diff-b187face62b4c9547cf843d1dd39c70ba1793c1741aa4b05b00b2ff34ae5a137L193-R200): Updated menu options and removed the `actualizarLogistica` method. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b187face62b4c9547cf843d1dd39c70ba1793c1741aa4b05b00b2ff34ae5a137L193-R200) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b187face62b4c9547cf843d1dd39c70ba1793c1741aa4b05b00b2ff34ae5a137L232-R232) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b187face62b4c9547cf843d1dd39c70ba1793c1741aa4b05b00b2ff34ae5a137L1351-L1355)

These changes enhance the functionality of the `MiFarma` project by enabling data persistence through file writing and improving the clarity of file handling operations.

author: bbinnick
body:
This pull request includes significant changes to the application, primarily focusing on adding new functionalities, enhancing user authentication, and managing game data. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme:

### Authentication and Routing Enhancements:

- Introduced `RequireAuth` component to protect routes and ensure only authenticated users can access certain pages. 
- Added new routes for `GameDetails` and `AdminGameManagement` pages.

### Dependency Updates:

- Added `typescript` as a development dependency.

### Component Additions and Modifications:

- Created a new component for managing games, including functionalities to add, edit, update, and delete games.
- Modified navigation buttons to include `Backlog` and `Admin` options, which are conditionally rendered based on user roles.

### Component Removals:

- Removed the `AddGameForm` component as its functionality has been integrated into the `AdminGameManagement` component.

### Minor Adjustments:

- Reorganized imports and removed unused components and data.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [charset-normalizer](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer) ([changelog](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)) | minor | `==3.3.2` -> `==3.4.5` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jawah/charset_normalizer (charset-normalizer)</summary>

### [`v3.4.5`](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#345-2026-03-06)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.4...3.4.5)

##### Changed

-   Update `setuptools` constraint to `setuptools>=68,<=82`.
-   Raised upper bound of mypyc for the optional pre-built extension to v1.19.1

##### Fixed

-   Add explicit link to lib math in our optimized build. ([#​692](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/692))
-   Logger level not restored correctly for empty byte sequences. ([#​701](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/701))
-   TypeError when passing bytearray to from_bytes. ([#​703](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/703))

##### Misc

-   Applied safe micro-optimizations in both our noise detector and language detector.
-   Rewrote the `query_yes_no` function (inside CLI) to avoid using ambiguous licensed code.
-   Added `cd.py` submodule into mypyc optional compilation to reduce further the performance impact.

### [`v3.4.4`](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#344-2025-10-13)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.3...3.4.4)

##### Changed

-   Bound `setuptools` to a specific constraint `setuptools>=68,<=81`.
-   Raised upper bound of mypyc for the optional pre-built extension to v1.18.2

##### Removed

-   `setuptools-scm` as a build dependency.

##### Misc

-   Enforced hashes in `dev-requirements.txt` and created `ci-requirements.txt` for security purposes.
-   Additional pre-built wheels for riscv64, s390x, and armv7l architectures.
-   Restore `  multiple.intoto.jsonl ` in GitHub releases in addition to individual attestation file per wheel.

### [`v3.4.3`](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#343-2025-08-09)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.2...3.4.3)

##### Changed

-   mypy(c) is no longer a required dependency at build time if `CHARSET_NORMALIZER_USE_MYPYC` isn't set to `1`. ([#​595](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/595)) ([#​583](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/583))
-   automatically lower confidence on small bytes samples that are not Unicode in `detect` output legacy function. ([#​391](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/391))

##### Added

-   Custom build backend to overcome inability to mark mypy as an optional dependency in the build phase.
-   Support for Python 3.14

##### Fixed

-   sdist archive contained useless directories.
-   automatically fallback on valid UTF-16 or UTF-32 even if the md says it's noisy. ([#​633](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/633))

##### Misc

-   SBOM are automatically published to the relevant GitHub release to comply with regulatory changes.
    Each published wheel comes with its SBOM. We choose CycloneDX as the format.
-   Prebuilt optimized wheel are no longer distributed by default for CPython 3.7 due to a change in cibuildwheel.

### [`v3.4.2`](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#342-2025-05-02)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.1...3.4.2)

##### Fixed

-   Addressed the DeprecationWarning in our CLI regarding `argparse.FileType` by backporting the target class into the package. ([#​591](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/591))
-   Improved the overall reliability of the detector with CJK Ideographs. ([#​605](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/605)) ([#​587](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/587))

##### Changed

-   Optional mypyc compilation upgraded to version 1.15 for Python >= 3.8

### [`v3.4.1`](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#341-2024-12-24)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/compare/3.4.0...3.4.1)

##### Changed

-   Project metadata are now stored using `pyproject.toml` instead of `setup.cfg` using setuptools as the build backend.
-   Enforce annotation delayed loading for a simpler and consistent types in the project.
-   Optional mypyc compilation upgraded to version 1.14 for Python >= 3.8

##### Added

-   pre-commit configuration.
-   noxfile.

##### Removed

-   `build-requirements.txt` as per using `pyproject.toml` native build configuration.
-   `bin/integration.py` and `bin/serve.py` in favor of downstream integration test (see noxfile).
-   `setup.cfg` in favor of `pyproject.toml` metadata configuration.
-   Unused `utils.range_scan` function.

##### Fixed

-   Converting content to Unicode bytes may insert `utf_8` instead of preferred `utf-8`. ([#​572](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/572))
-   Deprecation warning "'count' is passed as positional argument" when converting to Unicode bytes on Python 3.13+

### [`v3.4.0`](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#340-2024-10-08)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/compare/3.3.2...3.4.0)

##### Added

-   Argument `--no-preemptive` in the CLI to prevent the detector to search for hints.
-   Support for Python 3.13 ([#​512](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/512))

##### Fixed

-   Relax the TypeError exception thrown when trying to compare a CharsetMatch with anything else than a CharsetMatch.
-   Improved the general reliability of the detector based on user feedbacks. ([#​520](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/520)) ([#​509](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/509)) ([#​498](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/498)) ([#​407](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/407)) ([#​537](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/537))
-   Declared charset in content (preemptive detection) not changed when converting to utf-8 bytes. ([#​381](https://togithub.com/jawah/charset_normalizer/issues/381))

</details>

author: freddydk
body:
This PR is the first part of supporting GitHub Apps for authentication instead of PATs in GhTokenWorkflow.

After this PR, we still need a PAT for running the End 2 End tests, and we will have to have a PAT for End 2 End tests until we no longer support the versions, which doesn't support using GitHub Apps for authentication. The full scenario end 2 end test does use the GitHub app for authentication and does as such test that GhTokenWorkflow can be a GitHub app.

Also, the microsoft owned repositories used in end 2 end (bcsamples-*) are also using the PAT, as we currently do not have the GitHub App installed in the microsoft org. This will be part of a second part of this - to use the PAT in fewer places in the end 2 end tests.

body:
This pull request includes several changes to the `MiFarma` project, focusing on improving the user interface and updating user data. The most important changes include additions to the `VistaEmpleado` class, a new message prompt, and updates to the `usuariosGenerados.txt` file.

User Interface Improvements:

* [`MiFarma/VistaEmpleado.h`](diffhunk://#diff-b187face62b4c9547cf843d1dd39c70ba1793c1741aa4b05b00b2ff34ae5a137R1489-R1507): Added new elements to the user interface to enhance the display of user information, including setting cursor positions and drawing borders around user data.

User Data Updates:

* [`MiFarma/usuariosGenerados.txt`](diffhunk://#diff-95b483703ee9046d0391abd1c314d0dc40537e0dd751f6f6eff7fd8c05cf16dbL1-R10): Removed old user data entries and added new user data entries to update the list of generated users.

# UI and Theme Enhancements

This update introduces several improvements to the website's UI, theme, and structure to enhance usability, aesthetics, and maintainability.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2223198-039a-4158-bc28-0ce60c713a30)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f867e15-3deb-4acd-8017-535c94b32fbc)


## Changes Made

### 1. UI Improvements
- **Aspect Ratio Fix:** Adjusted the layout to maintain a proper aspect ratio across devices for a consistent user experience.
- **New Sections Added:**
  - **Core Members**: Showcasing the leadership team.
  - **Active Members**: Highlighting contributing members.
  - **Mentors**: Acknowledging the guidance provided by mentors.

### 2. Theme Enhancements
- **Improved Color Contrast:** Updated the base theme colors to ensure better visibility and compliance with accessibility standards.
- **Light Mode Redesign:** Redesigned the light mode theme to address visual inconsistencies and improve aesthetics.

### 3. Code Optimization
- **Static Member Data:** Replaced the JavaScript-based dynamic member information retrieval system with a direct indexing approach, improving performance and simplifying the codebase.

author: nameexhaustion
body:
Removes the division by 4 before clamping when calculating the async thread pool size.

This may benefit low core count systems, specifically those with less than 16 cores. Any potential performance gains may be observed particularly in systems with up to 7 cores, as the difference between having 1 vs 2 async threads is the most substantial.

| rayon threadpool size | old async thread count | new async thread count |
|-----------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 1                     | 1                      | 1                      |
| 2                     | 1                      | 2                      |
| 3                     | 1                      | 3                      |
| 4                     | 1                      | 4                      |
| 5                     | 1                      | 4                      |
| 6                     | 1                      | 4                      |
| 7                     | 1                      | 4                      |
| 8                     | 2                      | 4                      |
| 9                     | 2                      | 4                      |
| 10                    | 2                      | 4                      |
| 11                    | 2                      | 4                      |

author: kobzol
body:
This PR adds a new comparison mode to the compile result compare page. This mode allows users to compare the results between the LLVM and Cranelift backends if you are comparing the same commit against each other.

![llvm-vs-cranelift](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1e157c3-a89b-4608-82b7-f5d3ac07ddf8)

This was IMO the easiest way how to introduce this comparison mode. It would require non-trivial changes to get this working on the backend, and while this is arguably a bit of a hack, I think that it should work fine for the use-case that we need it for. In the future, this could be easily generalized to multiple backends, but for now it was not worth the hassle.

How to test:
1. Get results
```bash
$ rustup component add rustc-codegen-cranelift-preview --toolchain nightly
$ cargo run --bin collector -- bench_local `rustup +nightly which rustc` --include serde --profiles Debug --backends Llvm,Cranelift
```
2. Start the website (if you only have the data from the above run in the local DB, it should open the single commit compared against itself)
3. Click on "Self-compare backend"

author: techsmyth
body:
An important clean up of the logic around space authorization.

The logic whereby the space still used the account authorization was technical debt left over from when each account had exactly one space. 

This was 
a) a serious logic error in that having an elevated role on an account (e.g. org admin) gave access to all spaces in that account 
b) a blocker for space templates

[Whiteboard with rational + design notes](https://alkem.io/building-alkemio-org/challenges/technicaldesigns-9853/collaboration/knowledgebaselevelzerospa)

In addition, removed privileges related to auth + license reset on Space as we do not expose those mutations. 

To do: update test suites if needed.

body:
Howdy! This is my first contribution here, so please be kind. Just made some minor improvements to the types surrounding the type guards in `wrapper.ts`.

The following changes concern the  `isSignal`, `isComputed`, `isWatcher` functions:

- switched to standard function syntax instead of using `let` (now the actual brand checking logic is stored in an internal object)
- upgraded to bona fide type guards with `_ is T` return types
- removed the `any` parameter types
- added type parameters to  `isSignal` and `isComputed`
- wrapped the arguments with `Object` to prevent the `in` operator from throwing when it receives a primitive value

I also opted to switch the empty `#brand` methods to properties set to `true` in the `State`, `Computed`, and `Watcher` classes. This was solely done for aesthetics; for some reason those empty methods bothered me. If this is not desired, please let me know and I'll gladly revert those bits 😅

If there's anything I've overlooked (this was a late night PR) or anything else you'd like me to add to this changeset, please kindly let me know so I can address it promptly.

Thanks,

Nick

**Description:**

This pull request addresses two minor grammatical issues found in the Debian packaging documentation:

1. **"their builder"** was changed to **"Its builder"**: The original phrase used "their" when referring to "Launchpad", which is singular. The correct pronoun is "Its" to match the singular subject.
   
2. **"which Travis CI makes available to certain builds"** was changed to **"that Travis CI makes available to certain builds"**: The word "which" was replaced with "that" for better grammatical accuracy. "That" is the correct relative pronoun when referring to essential information about the subject.

These changes help ensure clarity and grammatical correctness in the documentation. Although these are small adjustments, they improve the overall quality of the documentation and ensure consistency in language usage.

body:
### Summary

This PR refactors the `Auth Controllers` and `Services` to implement the `Repository Pattern`, improving code organization, maintainability, and scalability. It also updates the routing structure for user creation, login and authentication operations.

---

### Approach

#### Refactor to Repository Pattern
- Shifted data access logic from controllers to dedicated repository classes.
- Refactored services to delegate database interactions to repositories, adhering to the principle of separation of concerns.
- Replaced direct database queries in controllers with service-layer methods for improved modularity.

#### Refactored User Controllers & Update API Endpoints
The following Endpoints have been updated and aligned with the repository pattern:
- **POST** `/api/auth/signup`: Endpoint for user registration.  
- **POST** `/api/auth/signin`: Endpoint for user login and session creation.  
- **GET** `/api/auth/signout`: Endpoint for user logout and session termination.  
- **GET** `/api/auth/verify`: Endpoint for verifying authentication tokens.  
- **POST** `/api/auth/forgot-password`: Endpoint for initiating the password recovery process.  
- **GET** `/api/auth/reset-password`: Endpoint for retrieving the password reset token or page.  
- **PATCH** `/api/auth/reset-password`: Endpoint for securely updating/resetting the user password.  

#### Monorepo Alignment
- Structured user-related logic into services and repositories for better codebase modularity.
- Updated route definitions to conform to the monorepo setup and ensure consistency.

---

author: jlowin
body:
This is a fun app that uses the API to pull public profiles + histories and uses them to seed the personalities and topics of two AI rappers.

www.battlesky.ai

### Edit

I'm going to close this because what was intended to be a silly app built on the public API became an external flashpoint for misinformation, which is disappointing. As the app itself indicates, it uses exclusively public data and neither stores that data nor uses it to train an LLM. It does not crawl Bluesky proactively, nor does it use the firehose. It is less invasive than a Bluesky client that allows you to bookmark posts. It is less invasive than a search engine. 

I understand that "AI", or perhaps a misunderstanding thereof, is the trigger here, but Bluesky (and more importantly the underlying protocol) is a public network. That's the entire appeal of it. I don't agree with the merit of the opinions expressed here, but their authors are welcome to hold them.

author: benjamsf
body:
# What
Add in configurations for elasticagent:
- Conditionally, with docker compose profile: kibana, run Elasticsearch and Kibana in the compose, so that you can tinker with logging in eg. a dev deployment.
- If the local setup is not used, then with injected token and url, ship logs to your preferred destination.

# How
elastic-agent-config/elastic-agent.yml
```
agent:
  id: ${ELASTIC_AGENT_ID}

# Fleet enrollment configuration
fleet:
  enabled: ${ELASTIC_AGENT_ENABLED}
  enrollment_token: ${ELASTIC_AGENT_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN}
  hosts:
    - ${ELASTIC_AGENT_FLEET_URL}

# Standalone configuration
outputs:
  default:
    type: elasticsearch
    hosts:
      - ${ELASTICSEARCH_HOSTS:-http://elasticsearch:9200}

inputs:
  - type: docker
    id: docker-logs
    enabled: ${LOG_INPUT_ENABLED:-true}
    streams:
      - containers.ids:
          - '*'  # Collect logs from all containers
    processors:
      - add_docker_metadata: ~
    # Enable the Docker module
    modules:
      - name: docker
        enabled: true

```
Then in ```docker-compose.yml```
Elasticagent like so:
```
  elastic-agent:
    image: docker.elastic.co/beats/elastic-agent:8.15.3
    container_name: elastic-agent
    environment:
      ELASTIC_AGENT_ENABLED: "${ELASTIC_AGENT_ENABLED:-false}"
      ELASTIC_AGENT_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN: "${ELASTIC_AGENT_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN}"
      ELASTIC_AGENT_FLEET_URL: "${ELASTIC_AGENT_FLEET_URL}"
      ELASTICSEARCH_HOSTS: "${ELASTICSEARCH_HOSTS:-http://elasticsearch:9200}"
      LOG_INPUT_ENABLED: "${LOG_INPUT_ENABLED:-true}"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /sys/fs/cgroup:/hostfs/sys/fs/cgroup
      - /proc:/hostfs/proc
      - /:/hostfs
      - ./elastic-agent-config/elastic-agent.yml:/usr/share/elastic-agent/elastic-agent.yml
    networks:
      - loggingnet
    restart: unless-stopped
```
TLDR ELASTIC_AGENT_ENABLED=true, if you want to enroll yourself to a Elastic fleet. If you don't, false, and local elk via using profile: kibana.

# Why
Logging is good for you
Tryout

author: ntfsvolume
body:
1. Redefine all TUI prompts into 3 levels: 

    - `basic_prompt.py` for standard prompts like `ask_file_path`, `enter_to_continue` or `ask_text`
    - `user_prompts.py` for CDL specific prompts like `import v4 config` or `extract cookies from browser`. These prompts could have nested prompts
    - `program_ui.py` with the class `ProgramUI` which contains all the custom user prompts of the program as methods
2. All prompts are now dynamically created passing a dict with the menu options and a mapping with the function that each option will execute
3. Remove all prompts that were unnecessary cause they were asking the same values as the config files. `Edit URLs.txt`, `Edit current config`, `Edit authentication config` and `Edit global config` are still present in the UI but now they just open the respective file in notepad or the default text editor of the OS
4. Switch back to using `os.system('cls')` to clear the screen on Windows. `rich.console.clear()` uses ANSI escape codes to clear the terminal and the legacy `cmd` does not support them. This let to prompts being rendered over leftover characters in the buffer.
5. `Browser_Cookies` options `browsers` and `sites` are now defined as lists in the config definition
6. Add `all` and `default` as hardcoded internal configs names. The user cannot create configs with those names. The idea with reserving `all` is for the user to pass it as a CLI argument to indicate that they want to run all configs sequentially. This will help to collapse some CLI arguments which are essentially duplicated cause they have a `single config` version and an `all config` version. None of the logic for this is implemented in this PR, they were just added as a reserved name

## Specify a non-root user in your Dockerfile

**This Pull Request was automatically generated by Jit.**
We highly recommend that you check the suggestion and make sure everything works before merging it.
An explanation of the suggested changes is available below.

### What changes are proposed in this Pull Request?

* First of all, check if your container is running as a root user. In most of the cases, you can do it by running a command like this: `docker run <image> whoami`. If it returns `root`, then you should consider using a non-root user, by following one of the next steps:
    * If a non-root user already exists in your container, consider using it.
    * If not, you can create a new user by adding a `USER` command to the Dockerfile, with a non-root user as argument, for example: `USER <non-root-user-name>`.

### Why are these changes important?

If you don't specify at least 1 USER command in the Dockerfile, the container will run as root. If a security vulnerability is exploited in the root container, an attacker could gain complete control over the host system and any other containers running on it, potentially leading to devastating consequences.

**Addressed Issue:**

Addressed notification and social media subsystems, improving their efficiency and maintainability. Specifically, it resolves redundant code and enhances data handling processes.

**What I Have Reengineered**

Notification Dispatch System:

Refactored logic for sending SMS messages to responders, eliminating redundant loops.
Added improved exception handling for API requests to the dispatchnotices endpoint.

Social Media Announcement Generator:

Optimized payloads for Facebook and Twitter announcements.
Reduced redundancy in creating crisis-related information.

Simplified the WebSocket broadcasting code and reduced redundant code.

Grouped reusable logic into helper functions.

**Reengineering Strategy or Approach Used**

Removing Redundant Code:

Extracted repetitive data processing (e.g., crisis description, type, and assistance formatting) into helper functions, improving maintainability.

Error Handling:

Enhanced exception handling around API calls.

Performance Improvement:

Reduced redundant loops and database queries to improve the speed.

**Impact of Changes**

Performance Gains:

Streamlined processing and reduced redundant steps, enhancing the system's response time.

Improved Maintainability:

The refactored code is modular, easier to understand, and aligns better with Django’s design principles.

Enhanced User Experience:

Notifications and social media posts are now consistently formatted and generated more efficiently.

author: atc0005
body:
## Overview

Add `CertificateChainIssues.WeakSignatureAlgorithm` field to surface weak signature algorithms used to sign certificates.

Weak signature algorithms include MD2, MD4, MD5, or SHA1.

These signature algorithms are known to be vulnerable to collision attacks. An attacker can exploit this to generate another certificate with the same digital signature, allowing an attacker to masquerade as the affected service.

NOTE: This does not apply to trusted root certificates; TLS clients trust them by their identity instead of the signature of their hash; client code setting this field would need to exclude root certificates from the determination whether the chain is vulnerable to weak signature algorithms.

## References

- fixes GH-38
- https://security.googleblog.com/2014/09/gradually-sunsetting-sha-1.html
- https://security.googleblog.com/2015/12/an-update-on-sha-1-certificates-in.html
- https://superuser.com/questions/1122069/why-are-root-cas-with-sha1-signatures-not-a-risk

author: tagatac
body:
<!-- Please add a title in the form of a great git commit message in the imperative mood (https://cbea.ms/git-commit/) -->

**What is changing**:
1. Disambiguate `Filename` and `Filepath` in the `Attachment` object.
2. Replace relative export paths with absolute ones.

**Why this change is being made**:
1. Previously, we were computing the absolute path of the attachments in multiple places in different ways depending on the options given and whether the attachment was converted or not. This was confusing and error prone (see #70).
2. As a result of the first change, we are using the copied path as the file to embed or reference. When embedding in PDFs, relative paths do not work, so we need to specify the copied path (under the export path in the case of the `--copy-attachments` option) as an absolute path.

**Related issue(s)**: Fixes #70 

**Follow-up changes needed**: None AFAIK

**Is the change completely covered by unit tests? If not, why not?**: No, similarly to converting the attachments path to an absolute path, we are not testing failures of the `filepath.Abs` function.

author: sthiber
body:
## Backend Changes
* Backend points for many GET, POST, and PUT requests.
* Added many new queries to the constant queries file.

## Frontend Changes
* In doctor dashboard I added functionality to the view schedule button in the dashboard.
* This will take you to a page where the doctor can see the appointments they have scheduled for the day.
* If it is after the appointment 30 min period, the appointment gets marked as 'Missed Appointment'
* If its during the appointment period, then the doctor is able to proceed with the appointment.
* If it is before the appointment period, it will not let the doctor proceed and it will inform the doctor.
* Proceeding to the appointment makes it where you get all the information on the patient, such as the appointment details, personal info, medical history, current medication, and previous appointments.
* You are able to prescribe medications.
* You are able to refill medications if the refill count is 0.
* You are able to write an after appointment message.
* You can charge the patient with specialty related charges, or you can make a custom charge and add it to the patient's bill. 

## DB Changes
* Made some modifications to the appointments table, removed visitTypeID. 
* Added 4 new tables for billing and charges, 'additional_charge_type' used for predefined values on the additional charges, specialty_additonal_charge table is used as a JOIN table, relates the charge with the specialty. bill_additional_charge, this keeps track of the additonal charges you make towards a bill. 'custom_charge' is used to keep up with custom_charges that the doctor makes and puts on the bill.
* Added visitNotesID to appointments table.


This took me forever so please try it out and find some bugs pls.

Task 2: Authentication Logic in the Auth Module
You will implement the authentication logic for the platform. The requirements are:
- Users can **sign up** and receive a JWT valid for **buyer operations** by default.
- Users can **log in** and receive a JWT valid for **buyer operations**.
- Users can switch roles (from buyer to seller and vice versa) using the `switchRole` mutation. This mutation will:
  - Accept the current JWT and return a new one valid for the opposite role (buyer ↔ seller).

Previous workflow failed, see logs: https://github.com/instructlab/ui/actions/runs/11862220666/job/33061144701#step:13:213.

The issue here was that the extracted tag data from one of the `"${{ steps.ghcr_ui_meta.outputs.tags }}"` values resolves to something like `quay.io/instructlab-ui/pathservice:main` where as the combined tags got only the image tag, resolving to `pr-334`. author: kunkelalexander
body:
# Version 3 of the spectral refinement criterion

## Explanation 
This pull request implements a refinement scheme based on the polynomial expansion underlying the FC-Gram algorithm. The accuracy of this polynomial expansion can be assessed by examining the decay rate of the polynomial coefficients. If the coefficients decay quickly, it implies that the higher-order terms of the polynomial contribute significantly less to the overall value, and truncating the expansion series after a few terms does not discard much information. Additionally, this property directly translates into the accuracy of the FC-Gram algorithm: The more important the higher-order terms in the polynomial expansion, the less accurate the periodic extension becomes.

We estimate the decay rate of the polynomial coefficients by checking the magnitude of the last $$N_{c}$$ coefficients, i.e. the 11th-, 12th- and 13-th order polynomial coefficient for $$N_{c}=3$$ and a 13th-order polynomial expansion. The grid is refined when at least one of these coefficients exceeds a threshold. The below figure showcases this refinement strategy for input functions with $N = 32$ points and an expansion in terms of polynomials up to order $$13$$. It indicates that a refinement threshold of around $$10^{-3}$$ for the last $$N_{c} = 2$$ coefficients may be suitable for achieving around $$6$$ points per wavelength. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea913579-d872-4b5c-8bce-998904e10d15)

While my tests indicate that this is true for simulations without gravity, we find that cosmological simulations with gravity and AMR require higher thresholds to avoid excessive refinement. In practice, we choose $N_{c} = 2$ coefficients and a threshold of $1$. Note that increasing $N_{c}$ makes the criterion more sensitive to higher resolutions, i.e. more than $20$ points per wavelength.

## Implementation

The pull request introduces the runtime variable `OPT__FLAG_SPECTRAL_N` that corresponds to $N_c$ in the explanation. It uses the `Refinement` column of the `Input__Flag_Spectral` file as refinement thresholds for the magnitude. 
Note that this pull request incorporates the spectral interpolation bugfix which should be reviewed first. (https://github.com/hyschive/gamer-fork/pull/128). 

## Tests

Tested with the Gaussian wave packet test, the light 2.8 Mpc/h and the heavy 2.8 Mpc/h halo as well as with the 5.6 Mpc/h box. Generally, a threshold of 1 tends to refine less than a threshold of 0 in [this pull request](https://github.com/hyschive/gamer-fork/pull/126).


### Small oscillations on homogeneous background

It does not seem to overly refine low-density regions with small oscillations. This is confirmed by the following plot:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49445d7c-e102-44c1-b598-12c4d46fe961)


It shows that small oscillations on a homogeneous background lead to small expansion coefficients even when they are fast. I experimented with normalizing the input data before computing the polynomial expansion as `normalized_data = (data - mean)/std_dev`. This does not work  for the following reason: A constant function with machine-precision noise will be normalised the zero and the noise will be scaled to order 1 which then leads to excessive refinement. 
In the current draft, this implies that the refinement thresholds need to be adapted based on the magnitude of the wave function in the simulation, i.e. a cosmological simulation scaled to a background density of 100, will need refinement thresholds that are 100 times higher. 

### Refinement of the light halo 
Evolving the light halo to z=0 on one spock node takes approximately two hours with a threshold of 1. 

![Data_000069_Lv_10_Slice_z_density_grid_x1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fa25714-63b2-4a42-838f-b5729cdc2a0f)
![Data_000069_Lv_10_Slice_z_density_grid_x5](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cf258a4e-c8e3-4d56-8fba-658f112b7257)

author: benedikthensen
body:
This pull request implements two changes:

- It fixes error messages which appeared if the sharing menu is closed while a player is joining or leaving. It now unsubscribes from the player join/leave events once it is closed and re-initializes itself when it is opened again.
- The sharing button on the UI now skips the connection screen and immediately opens the settings window of the session if it is already connected. This way, it is possible to open and close the collaborative settings menu throughout the collaborative session. Previously, the menu could only be opened during the connection process and was lost once the user closes it.

author: rachartier
body:
Hello,

`blink.cmp` has a module: `blink.compat`. This module is used to work with `nvim-cmp` sources but does not "emulate" all the functions present in `nvim-cmp`.

As a result, when the autocmds in the sidebar are set up and used (like quitting the sidebar), it is checked whether `require("cmp")` exists. With `blink.compat`, it does indeed exist, but the `get_sources` function used afterward does not, which causes an error: `Error executing lua callback: ...local/share/nvim/lazy/avante.nvim/lua/avante/sidebar.lua:1547: attempt to call method 'get_sources' (a nil value)`

This small fix adds a check for the `get_sources` method. If it does not exist, the rest of the function is aborted.

author: diogomene
body:
# What was done?
To address the code duplication identified in Joint-derived classes, an interface was introduced and implemented by the classes containing the repetitive routine. Subsequently, a method was added to the Joint class, which accepts as a parameter instances of classes inheriting from Joint and implementing the newly created interface.

This approach was chosen because the differences between the classes with the duplicated routine and those without it are minimal, making the abstraction of a new parent class unnecessary. A new class would have added only a few attributes and a single functionality, which would not have significantly improved code maintainability or readability.

All relevant Joint-derived classes now implement the ConstrainedBodiesJoint interface, ensuring the extracted initialization function can be applied uniformly.

As a result, code duplication has been reduced, and a clean mechanism for handling common initialization logic has been introduced. The inheritance structure remains unchanged, minimizing invasive modifications to the codebase while enhancing maintainability.

Resolve #301

body:
This PR identifies rockets (and rocket components) that are aerodynamically unstable, and does not set an open airframe warning in that case. The intent is to avoid spurious open airframe warnings on typical low power boosters after separation. If the booster is stable (as is the case for some high power boosters) the warning is set.

It also clarifies the wording of the warning itself; rather than simply stating that the airframe is open it states that this will case inaccurate altitude predictions.

Here's the warning as it appears currently, for the two stage rocket example:
![old-warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4cef42e-6c05-4a91-817e-142aa833ce22)

And here it is with this PR (note this example rocket is one for which the warning is relevant, so it still appears).
![new-warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d310df60-b323-4a93-a196-b2dfbbcc7dd7)

Fixes #2553

author: karolinaaaaaa
body:
Czas realizacji:
Na wykonanie zadania poświęciłam łącznie około 7 godzin. Czas ten obejmował zapoznanie się z wymaganiami, implementację, testowanie oraz wprowadzenie niezbędnych poprawek.

Feedback dotyczący zadania:
Zadanie było dobrze opisane, co umożliwiło realizację w odpowiednim tempie. Szczególnie doceniłam możliwość pracy z API NBP oraz integrację różnych komponentów w ramach aplikacji fullstack.  Ogólnie zadanie było super! :)

Moje podejście do zadania:
Podczas realizacji zadania skupiłam się na modularności, testowalności i utrzymaniu czytelnego kodu. Na backendzie zastosowałam zasady SOLID i DRY, tworząc serwis ExchangeRateService do pobierania i przetwarzania danych oraz klasę CurrencyFormatter do formatowania nazw walut. 

Na frontendzie wykorzystałam React i axios do dynamicznego wyświetlania danych. UI jest responsywne i dostosowane do zmieniających się danych, a użytkownik otrzymuje jasne komunikaty w przypadku błędów.

Przygotowałam testy jednostkowe i integracyjne, które pokrywają zarówno scenariusze sukcesu, jak i błędy. Skupiłam się na czytelności kodu i łatwości utrzymania projektu.

Dodatkowo można byłoby dodać:
Szczegółowe komunikaty błędów na frontendzie – obecnie są tylko ogólne komunikaty.
Logowanie błędów w backendzie – brak dedykowanego mechanizmu, takiego jak Monolog, do logowania błędów i wyjątków.
Cache danych API – aplikacja za każdym razem odpyta API NBP, nawet jeśli dane są już dostępne.
Zaawansowana walidacja na frontendzie – podstawowa walidacja istnieje, ale nie w pełni precyzyjna.

### Update [pycodestyle](https://pypi.org/project/pycodestyle) from **2.8.0** to **2.12.1**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.12.1
   ```
   -------------------

Changes:

* Properly preserve escaped `{` and `}` in fstrings in logical lines in 3.12+.
  PR 1252.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.12.0
   ```
   -------------------

Changes:

* E721: Fix false positive of the form `x.type(...) ==`.  PR 1228.
* E502: Fix false-negative with a backslash escape in a comment.  PR 1234.
* E204: New lint forbidding whitespace after decorator ``.  PR 1247.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.11.1
   ```
   -------------------

Changes:

* E275: fix false positive with fstrings containing keyword parts in python 3.12
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.11.0
   ```
   -------------------

Changes:

* Drop EOL python 3.6 / 3.7.  PR 1129, 1160.
* Add support for python 3.12.  PR 1147, 1148, 1152, 1153, 1154, 1163,
  1164, 1165, 1166, 1176, 1177, 1182.
* E721: adjust handling of type comparison.  Allowed forms are now
  ``isinstance(x, t)`` or ``type(x) is t``.  PR 1086, 1167.
* Remove handling of python 2 ``<>`` operator.  PR 1161.
* W606: removed.  ``async`` / ``await`` are always keywords.  PR 1162.
* Internal: move tests to pytest.  PR 1168, 1169, 1171, 1173, 1174, 1175.
* Remove handling of python 2 ``ur''`` strings.  PR 1181.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.10.0
   ```
   -------------------

Changes:

* E231: allow trailing comma inside 1-tuples in ``[]``.  PR 1108.
* W601, W602, W603, W604: removed (no longer relevant in python 3).  PR 1111.
* E741: also apply to lambdas.  PR 1106.
* E741: fix false positive for comparison operators.  PR 1118.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.9.1
   ```
   ------------------

Changes:

* E275: fix false positive for yield expressions.  PR 1091.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.9.0
   ```
   ------------------

Changes:

* E221, E222, E223, E224: add support for ``:=`` operator.  PR 1032.
* Drop python 2.7 / 3.5.
* E262: consider non-breaking spaces (``\xa0``) as whitespace.  PR 1035.
* Improve performance of ``_is_binary_operator``.  PR 1052.
* E275: requires whitespace around keywords.  PR 1063.
* Add support for python 3.11. PR 1070.
   ```
   
  
</details>


 

<details>
  <summary>Links</summary>
  
  - PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/pycodestyle
  - Changelog: https://data.safetycli.com/changelogs/pycodestyle/
  - Homepage: https://pycodestyle.pycqa.org/
</details>





### Update [pyflakes](https://pypi.org/project/pyflakes) from **2.4.0** to **3.2.0**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.2.0
   ```
   - Add support for ``*T`` (TypeVarTuple) and ``**P`` (ParamSpec) in PEP 695
  annotations.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.1.0
   ```
   - Drop support for EOL python 3.6 / 3.7
- Remove ``ContinueInFinally`` check (only relevant in python < 3.8)
- Fix forward annotations inside a nested scope
- Produce an error when a definition shadows an unused variable
- Fix accessed global annotation being redefined in a local scope
- Allow redefinition of functions across ``match`` arms
- Fix potential ``None`` for ``lineno`` during tokenization errors
- Add support for PEP 695 and python 3.12
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.0.1
   ```
   - Fix crash on augmented assign to ``print`` builtin
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.0.0
   ```
   - Detect undefined name in variable defined by an annotated assignment
- Add a new error for names which are annotated but unused
- Remove handling of python 2.x `` type:`` comments.  Use annotations instead
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.5.0
   ```
   - Drop support for EOL python 2.7 / 3.4 / 3.5
- Ignore ``__all__`` when not directly assigned
- Handle ``TypeAlias`` annotations as aliases (PEP 613)
- Assignment expressions (``:=``) target outer scope in comprehensions
- Add support for new python 3.11 syntax
- Unify output so it is always ``filename:lineno:col:  message``
- Properly report ``SyntaxError`` from stdin in python < 3.9
- Fix offsets of ``SyntaxError``s in pypy
   ```
   
  
</details>

body:
### Pull Request Description

**Title:** kevin/add-react

**Description:**

This pull request introduces several key updates to the project:

1. **React Integration**: Added React to the project, enabling the use of component-based architecture for better maintainability and scalability.

2. **MDX Support**: Integrated MDX, allowing for the combination of Markdown and JSX, which enhances the content authoring experience.

3. **Configuration Updates**: Updated various configuration files to accommodate the new dependencies and ensure smooth functionality.

4. **New Blog Post**: Added a blog post featuring the "First Letter Tool," which provides users with a unique way to interact with text.

5. **Responsive Design Enhancements**: Implemented support for extra small screen sizes, specifically adjusting the button layout on the "First Letter Tool" to improve usability on mobile devices.

These changes aim to enhance the overall user experience and provide a more robust framework for future development. Please review the modifications and provide any feedback.

Adds a `Monero oddities` section to the architecture book and adds an entry for https://github.com/Cuprate/cuprate/pull/342.
